metadata.title: Verification Oracles for Architectural and Insecure Design Deficiencies
observable_indicators: HTTP 200/201 on business transactions where client-altered pricing is accepted
Successful completion of terminal workflow states with skipped prerequisite tokens
Privilege elevation resulting from parameter modification in unvalidated requests
metadata.verification_oracle: status_code(terminal_action) in [200, 201] and prerequisite_state_completed == False or order.total == request.param_price

text: Observable indicators: a 200 response containing another user's email, tenant_id, account number, or document body; owner_id in the response differing from the authenticated principal; write operations returning 200/204 while the victim's record changes; list endpoints that omit ownership filtering. The oracle must not rely on UI rendering: assert that the response body contains a field value known to belong to the victim account. Differential testing between owner and non-owner sessions is the strongest signal.

metadata.title: CWE-283 Evidence Pattern: Unverified Resource Ownership
observable_indicators: HTTP 200 with victim-owned record fields
Response owner_id differs from session principal
Write succeeds on a foreign resource
List endpoint returns records outside the principal scope
metadata.verification_oracle: status_code == 200 and response.json().owner_id != session.user_id and response.json().id == victim_resource_id

text: Observable indicators: a 200 response containing a foreign tenant_id, account number, or personal data; sequential identifiers returning different users' records; body length or field sets that differ from the attacker's own-object baseline; write operations returning 200/204 while the victim object changes. Use differential assertions rather than UI inspection: compare the response object's tenant and owner fields against the authenticated session, and verify persistence with a follow-up read as the victim.

metadata.title: CWE-639 Evidence Pattern: IDOR and Object Key Substitution
observable_indicators: HTTP 200 containing another tenant's record
Sequential identifiers return other users' objects
Response length or field set differs from own-object baseline
Write operation succeeds on a foreign key
metadata.verification_oracle: status_code in (200, 204) and response.json().tenant_id != session.tenant_id

text: Observable indicators: a second use of the same reset token returns 200 and changes the password; the reset link host reflects an attacker-controlled Host or X-Forwarded-Host value; an OTP is accepted after many attempts without per-account lockout; response bodies or timings differ for known and unknown accounts. The strongest oracle is end-to-end: after replaying a token, authenticate as the victim with the newly set password. Log the token generation, consumption, and invalidation events to prove the lifecycle violation.

metadata.title: CWE-640 Evidence Pattern: Password Recovery Abuse
observable_indicators: Second use of a reset token returns 200
Reset link host reflects an attacker-controlled Host header
OTP accepted after many attempts without lockout
Different responses or timing for known and unknown accounts
metadata.verification_oracle: reset_response.status_code == 200 and login(victim_email, new_password) succeeds after token_reuse

text: Observable indicators: the response or a follow-up read shows the attacker-supplied owner_id or tenant_id; file metadata shows a uid or gid outside the service account; the victim can read an attacker-created resource; logout or release leaves ownership unchanged. Verify persistence independently of the create response, and compare the assigned owner against the authenticated principal. For filesystem cases, capture stat output and the upload path, and confirm whether a symlink changed the target of the ownership operation.

metadata.title: CWE-708 Evidence Pattern: Ownership Assignment Tampering
observable_indicators: Response shows an attacker-supplied owner_id
File uid or gid differs from the service account
Victim can access an attacker-created resource
Logout or release does not reset ownership
metadata.verification_oracle: created_record.owner_id == attacker_supplied_value and created_record.owner_id != session.user_id

text: Observable indicators: a 200 response to page_size=1000000 or a very large array; a resource count above the documented quota; a p95 latency spike under a small burst; the absence of 429 or 413 after the limit is crossed; degradation of a second legitimate account. Measure both the single-request amplification ratio and the aggregate effect. The oracle should combine business state (allocated_count > quota) with a timing or availability signal so that a merely slow response is not mistaken for exhaustion.

metadata.title: CWE-770 Evidence Pattern: Unbounded Resource Allocation
observable_indicators: HTTP 200 with page_size=1000000
Resource count exceeds the documented quota
p95 latency spike under a small burst
No 429 after the quota is exceeded
A second account is degraded
metadata.verification_oracle: request.status_code == 200 and allocated_count(principal) > quota and response_time_ms > baseline * 5

text: Observable indicators: a stale handle returns data after the release call; a second request observes uncommitted state; audit entries are duplicated or missing; a pooled connection is reused across tenants. Capture generation or version identifiers before and after release to prove that the object was recycled. For sessions, verify that logout followed by a parallel request still returns authenticated data. Reproduce under load and correlate timestamps to the release event.

metadata.title: CWE-826 Evidence Pattern: Premature Resource Release
observable_indicators: Stale handle returns data after release
A second request observes uncommitted state
Duplicate or missing audit entries
A pooled connection is reused across tenants
metadata.verification_oracle: stale_handle.read() returns data and stale_handle.generation != current_generation

text: Observable indicators: two or more 200 responses for a single-use action; a balance below zero; duplicate ledger rows for one business event; inventory oversold; audit logs showing interleaved reads before writes. Measure the delta from the expected single-execution outcome, not just the HTTP status. The strongest oracle combines a success count greater than one with a violated business invariant such as ledger sum or inventory count.

metadata.title: CWE-362 Evidence Pattern: Race Condition and Concurrent State Mutation
observable_indicators: Two or more 200 responses for a single-use action
Balance below zero
Duplicate ledger rows
Inventory oversold
Audit log shows interleaved reads
metadata.verification_oracle: count(success_responses) > 1 and ledger.delta != expected_delta

text: Observable indicators: the order total differs from the catalog calculation; an admin endpoint returns 200 without an admin role; an uploaded file type is accepted despite a client-side restriction; the response or a follow-up read reflects the tampered value. The oracle should compare server-persisted state with an independent recomputation, not with the client's submitted value. For role checks, verify access to a protected endpoint directly rather than relying on the presence of a hidden UI element.

metadata.title: CWE-602 Evidence Pattern: Client-Side Control Bypass
observable_indicators: Order total differs from the catalog calculation
Admin endpoint returns 200 without an admin role
Uploaded file type accepted despite a client check
Response reflects the tampered value
metadata.verification_oracle: server_order.total != catalog_price * quantity and order.status == 'confirmed'

text: Observable indicators: an admin endpoint returns 200 with a forged cookie; the response contains privileged data; X-Forwarded-For changes an IP-based access decision; a JWT with alg=none or a modified claim is accepted. The oracle should compare the effective authorization decision with the server-side session role, not with the client-supplied value. Verify with a protected action, and confirm that a fresh session without the forged input is denied.

metadata.title: CWE-807 Evidence Pattern: Untrusted Input in Security Decisions
observable_indicators: Admin endpoint returns 200 with a forged cookie
Response contains privileged data
X-Forwarded-For changes the access decision
A JWT with alg=none is accepted
metadata.verification_oracle: status_code == 200 and request.cookies['role'] == 'admin' and session.role != 'admin'

text: Observable indicators: the order total equals the tampered value; a profile user_id changes; a workflow status advances without its prerequisite; the response echoes the mutated hidden field. Compare the persisted value with an independent server-side calculation, and verify the effect on a follow-up read or a second workflow step. The oracle should assert both the tampered value and the divergence from the authoritative value so that a legitimate discount is not misclassified.

metadata.title: CWE-472 Evidence Pattern: Assumed-Immutable Parameter Tampering
observable_indicators: Order total equals the tampered value
Profile user_id changed
Status advanced without a prerequisite
Response echoes the mutated hidden field
metadata.verification_oracle: order.total == tampered_total and order.total != catalog_total

text: Observable indicators: the response shows role=admin or is_admin=true; the balance changes; tenant_id is altered; a subsequent administrative request succeeds. Verify persistence in a fresh session so that a transient response echo is not mistaken for a stored change. The oracle should compare the persisted role or balance with the pre-request value and with the authenticated principal's legitimate entitlement.

metadata.title: CWE-915 Evidence Pattern: Mass Assignment
observable_indicators: Response shows role=admin or is_admin=true
Balance changed
tenant_id altered
A subsequent admin request succeeds
metadata.verification_oracle: response.json().role == 'admin' and session.role != 'admin'

text: Observable indicators: login succeeds with a 0e hash collision; a token prefix is accepted; a case variant grants a role; response time correlates with the correct prefix. The oracle should assert both successful access and inequality between the supplied and stored values. For timing, collect enough samples to distinguish a real correlation from noise, and confirm the bypass with a protected action rather than a response message alone.

metadata.title: CWE-697 Evidence Pattern: Comparison Logic Bypass
observable_indicators: Login succeeds with a 0e hash collision
A token prefix is accepted
A case variant grants a role
Response time correlates with the correct prefix
metadata.verification_oracle: auth_success == true and supplied_value != stored_value

text: Observable indicators: the post-login session identifier equals the pre-login identifier; the attacker session gains authenticated access using the planted identifier; a session identifier appears in the URL; the old identifier remains valid after logout. The oracle should compare the identifier before and after authentication and confirm access to a protected endpoint from the attacker's browser. Capture Set-Cookie and Location headers to prove whether rotation occurred.

metadata.title: CWE-384 Evidence Pattern: Session Identifier Fixation
observable_indicators: Post-login session ID equals the pre-login ID
Attacker session gains authenticated access with the planted ID
URL contains a session identifier
Old identifier remains valid after logout
metadata.verification_oracle: pre_auth_sid == post_auth_sid and authenticated == true and protected_endpoint.status_code == 200

text: Observable indicators: a 200 response after the current-password field is removed; login succeeds with the new password; the old password fails; other sessions remain authenticated; the request succeeds without a CSRF token. The oracle should combine the change response with a successful login using the new credential, and confirm that the old credential is rejected. For CSRF, verify that a cross-origin request without the token also succeeds.

metadata.title: CWE-620 Evidence Pattern: Password Change Without Re-authentication
observable_indicators: HTTP 200 after removing the current-password field
Login succeeds with the new password
Old password no longer works
Other sessions remain authenticated
No CSRF token required
metadata.verification_oracle: change_response.status_code == 200 and login(user, new_password).status_code == 200 and 'current_password' not in request.body

text: Observable indicators: a CPU or memory spike from a single small request; a sharp p95 latency increase; 503 or timeout under a small burst; fail-open behavior during exhaustion; a connection pool fully consumed. Measure the amplification ratio (server work divided by request bytes) and confirm impact on a separate legitimate user. The oracle should combine a resource signal with a second-user availability signal so that a merely slow endpoint is not misclassified.

metadata.title: CWE-400 Evidence Pattern: Resource Exhaustion Amplification
observable_indicators: CPU or memory spike from a single small request
p95 latency increases sharply
503 or timeout under a small burst
Fail-open behavior during exhaustion
Connection pool fully consumed
metadata.verification_oracle: amplification_ratio > 100 and service.error_rate > 0.5 and second_user.request.status_code >= 500

text: Observable indicators: deadlock under two concurrent operations; a double-unlock error or panic; worker threads stuck on a lock; an attacker-created lock file blocks the service; inconsistent resource state. Capture thread dumps or lock traces to prove the ordering inversion. The oracle should combine concurrency with a latency or error threshold, and verify that a single request succeeds while the interleaved pair does not.

metadata.title: CWE-667 Evidence Pattern: Locking Discipline Failure
observable_indicators: Deadlock under two concurrent operations
Double-unlock error or panic
Worker threads stuck on a lock
Attacker-created lock file blocks the service
Inconsistent resource state
metadata.verification_oracle: concurrent_requests > 1 and median_latency > timeout and error_rate > 0.5

text: Observable indicators: an unconsidered scheme such as ftp is accepted; a prefix-matched path exposes a sibling resource; a foreign tenant object passes the check; a case or encoding variant bypasses the comparison. The oracle should assert both acceptance and the presence of a factor that should have caused rejection. Confirm with a protected action rather than a response message alone.

metadata.title: CWE-1023 Evidence Pattern: Missing-Factor Comparison Bypass
observable_indicators: ftp:// or another unconsidered scheme is accepted
A prefix-matched path exposes a sibling resource
A foreign tenant object passes the check
Case or encoding variant bypasses the comparison
metadata.verification_oracle: request.accepted == true and request.scheme not in allowlist and protected_resource.status_code == 200

text: Observable indicators: the response contains a marker string from a file outside the web root, such as root:x:0:0 or [fonts] from win.ini; an error message reveals an absolute path; an encoded traversal variant returns a different body than the plain filename; writing to a template or configuration file changes subsequent behavior. The oracle should assert that a marker unique to the out-of-root file is present while the request contained a traversal sequence, and that the same request against a patched build returns a uniform error.

metadata.title: CWE-22 Evidence Pattern: Path Traversal
observable_indicators: Response contains contents of a file outside the web root
Error message reveals an absolute filesystem path
Encoded traversal returns a different body than the plain name
Write to a template or config file changes application behavior
metadata.verification_oracle: response.status_code == 200 and known_marker_of('/etc/passwd' or 'win.ini') in response.body and requested_name contains traversal_sequence

text: Observable indicators: a time delay proportional to an injected sleep value; an out-of-band DNS or HTTP interaction from the target host; command output such as uid=33(www-data) reflected in the response; an unexpected child process spawned by the web service account; error text naming a shell or command absent from the code path. The strongest oracle is an out-of-band callback, because it proves execution without depending on output handling. Time-based confirmation should use a value large enough to exceed normal jitter and be repeated to exclude coincidence.

metadata.title: CWE-78 Evidence Pattern: OS Command Injection
observable_indicators: Time delay proportional to a sleep value
Out-of-band DNS or HTTP interaction
Command output reflected in the response
Unexpected child process spawned by the web service
Error text naming a shell or command not in the code path
metadata.verification_oracle: elapsed_ms >= injected_sleep_seconds * 1000 and baseline_ms < 1000, or collaborator.hit(source=target)

text: Observable indicators: database error text in the response; a body-length difference between true and false boolean payloads; a time delay proportional to a sleep payload; UNION output containing rows from another table; a login that succeeds with a tautology and no valid password. Prefer differential and time-based evidence when output is suppressed. The oracle should combine a payload that provably changed the query's truth value or execution time with confirmation that a legitimate payload of the same shape does not, and should be repeated to exclude noise.

metadata.title: CWE-89 Evidence Pattern: SQL Injection
observable_indicators: Database error text in the response
Different body length for true versus false boolean payloads
Time delay proportional to a sleep payload
UNION output containing data from another table
Login succeeds with a tautology and no valid password
metadata.verification_oracle: response.body contains db_error_signature or (elapsed_ms >= sleep_ms and baseline_ms < 500) or login_success_with('\' OR 1=1 --')

text: Observable indicators: script executes in the target origin; the payload appears unencoded in the response body; a DOM sink receives attacker-controlled data; Content-Security-Policy is absent or allows unsafe-inline; the session cookie is readable by JavaScript. Confirmation should occur in a real browser so that context, encoding, and CSP are all exercised. The oracle asserts execution in the target origin rather than mere reflection, because reflected markup may still be inert. An out-of-band callback proves execution even when a visible alert is blocked.

metadata.title: CWE-79 Evidence Pattern: Cross-Site Scripting
observable_indicators: Script executes in the target origin
Payload appears unencoded in the response body
DOM sink receives attacker-controlled data
CSP absent or allows unsafe-inline
Session cookie accessible to JavaScript
metadata.verification_oracle: browser.alert_fired == true and document.domain == target_origin, or collaborator.hit(source=victim_browser)

text: Observable indicators: an out-of-band callback fires during deserialization; an unexpected process or file appears; an error names a gadget class or library version; serialized magic bytes are accepted from the client in a cookie or body; a crafted chain produces a predictable time delay. The strongest oracle is an out-of-band interaction triggered specifically by the blob, because it proves execution rather than mere parsing. Capture the pre-delivery baseline so that normal background callbacks are excluded, and confirm that an equivalent non-gadget blob does not trigger the same effect.

metadata.title: CWE-502 Evidence Pattern: Insecure Deserialization
observable_indicators: Out-of-band callback during deserialization
Unexpected process or file created
Deserialization error naming a gadget class
Serialized magic bytes accepted from the client
Time delay from a crafted chain
metadata.verification_oracle: collaborator.hit(source=target) during deserialize_request or process_exists('calc') after blob_delivery

text: Observable indicators: the victim's resource changes after a cross-origin auto-submit; a request with no token, an empty token, or another user's token succeeds; the session cookie lacks SameSite; a GET request mutates state. The oracle compares server-side state before and after the forged request and confirms the request originated from a different origin. Capture the cross-origin request and the resulting state change as a pair, and verify that a request with a valid token and matching Origin does not trigger the same anomaly.

metadata.title: CWE-352 Evidence Pattern: CSRF
observable_indicators: State changed after a cross-origin auto-submit
Request succeeds with no token or a static token
SameSite attribute absent on the session cookie
GET request mutates state
metadata.verification_oracle: victim_resource.state != pre_state and request.origin != target_origin and request.cookies includes session

text: Observable indicators: an uploaded executable file is served and executed; the server executes code embedded in an image; the stored filename retains a dangerous extension; the upload response reveals a path inside the web root; an SVG or HTML upload renders script when viewed. The oracle should request the stored file and assert that a marker placed in the payload is executed or rendered, not merely stored. Confirm the storage path and handler mapping so that the finding is attributed to execution rather than reflection.

metadata.title: CWE-434 Evidence Pattern: Unrestricted File Upload
observable_indicators: Uploaded executable file is served and executed
Server executes code from an uploaded image
Stored filename retains a dangerous extension
Upload response reveals a path inside the web root
SVG or HTML upload renders script
metadata.verification_oracle: upload.status_code == 200 and GET(stored_url).body contains marker_output and stored_extension in dangerous_set

text: Observable indicators: the response contains contents of a local file; an out-of-band DNS or HTTP callback originates from the parser; a parser error names a resolved external URI; memory or CPU spikes from recursive entity expansion; a SAML or SVG upload triggers an external fetch. The oracle should assert a marker unique to the referenced file or a callback tied to the specific document. Because XXE often fails silently, out-of-band evidence is stronger than reflected output, and the callback should be correlated to the exact request.

metadata.title: CWE-611 Evidence Pattern: XML External Entity Injection
observable_indicators: Response contains local file contents
Out-of-band DNS or HTTP callback from the parser
Parser error naming a resolved external URI
Memory or CPU spike from entity expansion
SAML or SVG upload triggers external fetch
metadata.verification_oracle: response.body contains known_marker_of('file:///etc/passwd') or collaborator.hit(source=target)

text: Observable indicators: the response returns content from an internal service; cloud metadata credentials appear in the response; an out-of-band callback originates from the server; timing differs between reachable and filtered ports; a redirect to an internal host is followed. The oracle should tie the response or callback to a destination that resolves into a private, loopback, link-local, or metadata range, and confirm that the same feature rejects a control URL outside the allowlist. Port-scan inference via timing is weaker evidence and should be corroborated.

metadata.title: CWE-918 Evidence Pattern: SSRF
observable_indicators: Response returns internal service content
Cloud metadata credentials in the response
Out-of-band callback from the server
Timing difference between reachable and filtered ports
Redirect to an internal host followed
metadata.verification_oracle: response.body contains 'iam/security-credentials' or internal_service_banner, or collaborator.hit(source=target) and requested_host resolves to private_range

text: Observable indicators: response time grows exponentially with input length for a specific character pattern; CPU saturates from a single request; worker timeouts occur under a small burst; a second user experiences latency; no input length limit is enforced. The oracle should measure a scaling curve rather than a single slow response, because a one-off delay may be incidental. Compare the crafted input against a benign string of the same length, and confirm that the delay disappears with a patched pattern or a configured backtracking limit.

metadata.title: CWE-1333 Evidence Pattern: ReDoS
observable_indicators: Response time grows exponentially with input length
CPU saturation from a single request
Worker timeout under a small burst
Second user experiences latency
No input length limit enforced
metadata.verification_oracle: time(n+5) / time(n) > 2 for crafted_string and cpu_usage > 0.9 and second_user.latency > baseline * 5

text: Observable indicators: a credential-bearing POST observed on port 80; a login form action using http://; a password field submitted to a non-TLS third party; a session cookie issued without the Secure flag; an absent HSTS header. The oracle should match a request that carries a credential parameter over cleartext, not merely an HTTP page load. Capture the raw request line, host, and body, and pair it with a successful authentication replay to demonstrate impact.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-01: Cleartext Credential Transmission Evidence
observable_indicators: Credential POST observed over TCP port 80
Login form action uses http://
Password field submitted to a non-TLS third party
Session cookie issued without Secure
HSTS header absent
metadata.verification_oracle: request.scheme == 'http' and any(k in body for k in ['password','passwd','otp','token'])

text: Observable indicators: a successful login with a documented default pair; an administrative console reachable from an untrusted network; no forced password change on first login; a demo account authenticating in production. The oracle must confirm authentication and the resulting role, not merely a 200 response, because some applications return a generic page for invalid logins. Record the exact credential source and the component version so the finding is reproducible.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-02: Default Credential Acceptance Evidence
observable_indicators: Successful login with a documented default pair
Admin console reachable from an untrusted network
No forced password change on first login
Demo account authenticates in production
metadata.verification_oracle: login(username=default_user, password=default_pass).status == 200 and session.role == 'admin'

text: Observable indicators: hundreds of failures with no delay or lock; the threshold resetting after a cookie or header change; lockout triggered by username alone; no MFA challenge after an anomalous success; distributed attempts showing constant response time. The oracle should combine a high failure count with the absence of any throttling signal, and pair it with a successful guess to show exploitability. For lockout abuse, show that a victim account can be locked repeatedly without authentication.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-03: Attempt-Limit Bypass Evidence
observable_indicators: Hundreds of failures with no delay or lock
Threshold resets after cookie or header change
Lockout triggered by username alone
No MFA challenge after anomalous success
Distributed attempts show constant response time
metadata.verification_oracle: failed_attempts >= 100 and response_time_delta < 50ms and no lockout_state

text: Observable indicators: a protected page or API returns 200 without a session; a method or path variant reaches the handler; a client flag toggles the interface; an alternate host serves the protected route. The oracle should assert access to protected data or a protected action with no authenticated session and no client-controlled identity input. Capture the exact request shape that bypassed the filter and verify that the canonical request is denied.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-04: Unauthenticated Protected-Action Evidence
observable_indicators: Protected page returns 200 without a session
Protected API returns data without authentication
Method or path variant reaches the handler
Client flag toggles the interface
Alternate host serves the protected route
metadata.verification_oracle: request.cookies == {} and endpoint.status_code == 200 and endpoint.body contains protected_marker

text: Observable indicators: the cookie decodes to a password or username-derived hash; the token remains valid after logout or password change; the same token is accepted from a second device; the token is unchanged across sessions. The oracle should prove durable access by replaying the cookie after a revocation event and reaching an authenticated endpoint. Record the decoded structure without exposing real user secrets in the report.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-05: Persistent Token Weakness Evidence
observable_indicators: Cookie decodes to a password or username hash
Token remains valid after logout
Token remains valid after password change
Same token accepted from a second device
Token unchanged across sessions
metadata.verification_oracle: replay_cookie.status == 200 and logout_occurred == true and password_changed == true

text: Observable indicators: a sensitive page renders after logout via the Back button; the response lacks Cache-Control no-store; a proxy serves a personalized page to another user; history retains a one-time code; autocomplete repopulates a password or OTP. The oracle should reproduce content recovery after a logout event and tie it to a missing directive. Capture the header and the recovered body together so the finding is unambiguous.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-06: Cached Authenticated Content Evidence
observable_indicators: Sensitive page renders after logout via Back
Response lacks Cache-Control: no-store
Proxy serves a personalized page to another user
History retains a one-time code
Autocomplete repopulates a password or OTP
metadata.verification_oracle: logout_performed == true and back_navigation.body contains account_marker and response.headers['Cache-Control'] lacks 'no-store'

text: Observable indicators: Password123 or a one-character password accepted; the client meter shows weak but the server accepts; no breached-password rejection; the reset path weaker than registration. The oracle should confirm acceptance by authenticating with the weak password, not by reading a strength meter. Test through a direct request to exclude client-side enforcement, and record the exact policy boundary that failed.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-07: Weak Password Acceptance Evidence
observable_indicators: Password123 accepted
One-character password accepted
Client shows weak but server accepts
No breached-password rejection
Reset path weaker than registration
metadata.verification_oracle: create_user(password='Password123').status == 200 and login(new_user, 'Password123').status == 200

text: Observable indicators: recovery succeeds with a researched answer; unlimited answer attempts; a case or whitespace variant accepted; recovery bypasses MFA; the same answer works across accounts. The oracle should complete the reset and authenticate as the victim, and should measure attempts to show the absence of throttling. Record which question and normalization allowed the bypass.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-08: Security Question Bypass Evidence
observable_indicators: Recovery succeeds with a researched answer
Unlimited answer attempts
Case or whitespace variant accepted
Recovery bypasses MFA
Same answer works across accounts
metadata.verification_oracle: reset_completed == true and attempts > 20 and no_rate_limit_triggered

text: Observable indicators: a token accepted twice; a reset link pointing to an attacker host; a change succeeding without the current password; an old session remaining valid; a predictable or long-lived token. The oracle should perform a second reset with the same token and authenticate with the resulting password, and separately verify that a pre-change session still reaches protected data. Capture headers and token values without exposing live secrets.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-09: Reset and Change Weakness Evidence
observable_indicators: Token accepted twice
Reset link points to an attacker host
Change succeeds without current password
Old session remains valid
Token predictable or long-lived
metadata.verification_oracle: second_reset.status == 200 and login(victim, new_password2).status == 200

text: Observable indicators: an API issues a session without MFA; support resets after weak verification; a legacy endpoint accepts a retired credential type; the same account has different policies per channel; no alert fires when a weak channel is used. The oracle should compare the factor requirements across channels for one account and demonstrate a session issued with fewer factors. Capture the channel, the request, and the resulting session scope.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-10: Weaker Channel Authentication Evidence
observable_indicators: API issues a session without MFA
Support resets after weak verification
Legacy endpoint accepts a retired credential type
Same account has different policies per channel
No alert when a weak channel is used
metadata.verification_oracle: api_login(username, password).status == 200 and session.mfa_verified == false and web_login_requires_mfa == true

text: Observable indicators: identifier entropy below 128 bits; sequential or timestamp-based identifiers; client-side state accepted without a signature; a session valid after the stated timeout; the identifier unchanged after login. The oracle should combine statistical weakness with a practical validation, such as a forged state value returning another user's data. Capture the sample and the analysis output so the finding is reproducible.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-01: Session Schema Weakness Evidence
observable_indicators: Identifier entropy below 128 bits
Sequential or timestamp-based identifiers
Client-side state accepted without signature
Session valid after the stated timeout
Identifier unchanged after login
metadata.verification_oracle: entropy_bits(sample) < 128 or decoded_state.user_id != session.user_id and request.status == 200

text: Observable indicators: Set-Cookie lacking Secure or HttpOnly; SameSite absent or None; Domain set to a parent domain on a session cookie; expiry far beyond policy. The oracle should match a session-bearing cookie, not a harmless preference cookie, and pair the finding with a practical consequence such as script readability or cleartext transmission.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-02: Cookie Flag Deficiency Evidence
observable_indicators: Set-Cookie lacks Secure
Set-Cookie lacks HttpOnly
SameSite absent or None
Domain=.example.com on a session cookie
Expiry far beyond session policy

text: Observable indicators: an order response whose total is negative or differs from unit_price * quantity; a balance or store credit that increases after a purchase; HTTP 200/201 for quantity=-1, quantity=0, or quantity far above stock; allocation failure or timeout that scales with the submitted quantity; inventory decremented by a different amount than requested. The oracle must read server-side state, not the UI: assert that the persisted order total equals the independently computed price and that the payment ledger debit is positive. Differential comparison between quantity=1 and quantity=-1 is the strongest signal.

metadata.verification_oracle: status_code in (200, 201) and order.total == unit_price * quantity and order.total >= 0 and ledger.debit > 0
